hypothesis: Compounding profits into additional lots each month — net of 30% STCG tax, slippage at scale, and a cliff-edge drawdown brake — grows ₹20k-₹50k of starting capital into a multi-lakh account over 2023-2025, and the cliff-edge brake is an adequate drawdown control.

config.base_stack: P70_L40d adaptive ATR regime filter + VIX×1.1 dynamic IV + VIX tilt sizing (sweet 1.5x / danger 0.5x / else 1x)
config.slippage_rule: ₹2/unit extra spread per lot above 10 lots per trade
config.lot_sizing_rule: lots = min(max(1, floor(net_capital × 0.30 / premium_per_lot)), max_lots_cap); lots = 1 whenever the drawdown brake is engaged
config.brake_rule: If (peak_net_capital - net_capital) / peak_net_capital >= 0.35 at month close, freeze lots at 1. Brake clears only when net_capital exceeds the prior peak.
config.tax_rule: 30% of each profitable month's P&L moved to tax_reserve; reserve excluded from sizing capital

FINDING-1.title: The cliff-edge drawdown brake is a capital trap, not a capital control
FINDING-1.detail: The brake freezes lot count at 1 once drawdown reaches 35% from the high-water mark, and clears only when net capital exceeds the prior peak. At 1 lot the engine cannot generate enough P&L to climb back to a peak set at a far larger lot count, so the freeze is effectively permanent. Triggered in Dec 2023 and held for 22 months to the end of the simulation. This is the finding that motivated EXP-0017 and it is consistent across both conflicting source records.
FINDING-1.confidence: HIGH — qualitative, corroborated by both sources and by direct reading of the brake logic in the committed script

FINDING-2.title: Recovery requires partial operation, not minimum operation
FINDING-2.detail: Because the brake's release condition is tied to the old peak while its action removes the capacity needed to reach that peak, any drawdown control that collapses to a floor must also provide a path back. EXP-0017 confirmed this by showing the step-down 4-tier design recovering to 1.00x by Jul 2024 over the same trade set.
FINDING-2.confidence: HIGH — superseded and confirmed by EXP-0017

FINDING-3.title: Monthly tax withholding materially changes the compounding path
FINDING-3.detail: Withholding 30% of each profitable month's P&L from sizing capital both lowers the lot count every subsequent month and lowers the high-water mark that the drawdown brake measures against, so the tax model interacts with the risk control rather than merely scaling the result. Magnitude unquantified in this record.
FINDING-3.confidence: LOW — mechanism is clear from the script; no trustworthy numbers to size the effect

conclusion: HYPOTHESIS PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, with the risk-control half REJECTED. Compounding does convert a small starting account into a multi-lakh one over 2023-2025, but the cliff-edge drawdown brake is unfit for purpose: it froze the engine at 1 lot in Dec 2023 and never released, because its release condition depends on recovering a high-water mark that the freeze itself makes unreachable. This rejection is the sole reason EXP-0017 was run, and EXP-0017's step-down 4-tier design superseded it. The specific capital figures from this experiment are not recoverable from the surviving records, which disagree by about 6x; they must be regenerated before any EXP-0016 number is quoted anywhere.
caveats: CAVEAT-1: Post-hoc sizing replay, not a true re-backtest. Like EXP-0015 and EXP-0017, this replays the same ~1,522 one-lot trades with a sizing multiplier applied, assuming per-lot P&L is independent of position size. Invalid beyond roughly 15-20 lots, where the order moves the book (HANDOFF.md G1).
CAVEAT-2: The ₹500 premium-per-lot floor caps lot counts when deep-OTM options appear, so live lot counts may come out lower than simulated (HANDOFF.md G2).
CAVEAT-3: The drawdown brake is evaluated at month close only, so intraday and intra-month breaches of the 35% threshold are invisible to it (related to RISK-8).
CAVEAT-4: Tax is modeled as a flat 30% STCG withholding; actual liability at ITR filing will differ.
